name: Imipenem+cilastatin
executiveSummary: Carbapenem + cilastatin. Adult **500 mg IV every 6 h** (as imipenem); severe/Pseudomonas **1 g every 6–8 h** (usual max **4 g/day**). Pediatrics **15–25 mg/kg every 6 h** (**60–100 mg/kg/day**).
indications:
## Indications

- Severe polymicrobial / MDR Gram-negative infections (respiratory, urinary, intra-abdominal, bone, skin, sepsis) when spectrum is justified.
- Not first-line for meningitis (penetration and seizures).

## Precautions

- Higher seizure risk than other carbapenems — avoid in CNS disease/severe renal failure if alternatives exist.
- **Do not combine with ganciclovir** (seizures).
- Strict renal adjustment. Avoid in neonates unless specialist decision.

> Doses expressed as **imipenem**; cilastatin 1:1.

adulto.dose: Usual: **500 mg IV every 6 h**. Severe / Pseudomonas: **1 g every 6–8 h**. Usual max **4 g/day** imipenem. Mandatory renal adjustment.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with ~10 mL NS/D5W; dilute in ~100 mL (≈5 mg/mL). ≤500 mg over **20–30 min**; >500 mg over **40–60 min**. Slow if nausea.
adulto.notes: ~37.5 mg Na+ per 500 mg. IM possible in selected regimens.

pediatrico.dose: **15–25 mg/kg every 6 h** (**60–100 mg/kg/day**); max **2–4 g/day** by severity. CF: up to **~90 mg/kg/day** every 6 h (max **4 g/day**).
pediatrico.administration: IV 15–60 min by dose; diluent NS/D5–10%.
pediatrico.notes: Not advised in newborns. Avoid coadministration with ganciclovir.

neonatal.dose: Not routine; only if ID/NNU directs with local table.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: up to ~24 h refrigerated (label).
- Diluted NS: ~4 h room temp / ~48 h refrigerated; D5W: ~4 h room temp / ~24 h refrigerated.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, phlebitis, rash, seizures, *C. difficile*; rare: leukopenia, hepato/nephrotoxicity.
